evidence: Additive after 0083: no table, column, policy, function, grant or applied migration is removed or rewritten; the code at the W05b release keeps working on the new schema, since it calls none of the new commands. 0084 adds identity.patient_emergency_contacts, identity.emergency_contact_verifications, identity.emergency_contact_notifications and identity.facility_alert_phones (append-only, revoked from PUBLIC, no runtime table privilege except SELECT on the facility alert phones for hid_identity_runtime), the patient commands, the Identity-system delivery claim and outcome commands, identity.admin_set_facility_alert_phone (platform.facility.manage) and identity.admin_opt_out_emergency_contact (the new permission platform.emergency-contact.manage, inserted with its role rows for support_admin and every role holding platform.principal.manage), all SECURITY DEFINER with pinned search_path; it grants EXECUTE on them to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime where those roles exist, and never grants the audit helper or the trigger function. Its last statement adds the AFTER INSERT trigger emergency_contact_notification_intent on identity.outbox_events with WHEN (new.event_type = 'EmergencyAccessActivated'); the trigger creates intents only for verified contacts with alerts on (none can exist before delivery is enabled), and its own failure, its failure audit included, never fails break-glass. Break-glass authorization itself is unchanged. Locks until commit: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities, auth.accounts, identity.patients, identity.consent_grants and identity.outbox_events (writes wait, reads do not), all taken by its first statement in that order, the order in which organization approval, registration, NIN registration and break-glass write them, so none of them can deadlock with it (a registration and an organization approval raced against the migration runner on PostgreSQL 16 each deadlocked with the locks taken statement by statement and completed with them taken up front); outbox writes therefore wait for the whole migration; ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.permissions, auth.role_permissions and audit.events and ROW SHARE on auth.roles and auth.permissions (block no reader or writer); about 130 ms on an empty PostgreSQL 16 database, measured with pg_locks; the dry run holds the same locks together. runtime-grants.sql adds the same EXECUTE and SELECT grants and the revokes for a later role bootstrap (without them a bootstrap strips the grants); the release does not apply it. Built 0001-0084 on PostgreSQL 16 in production order (0001-0072, role bootstrap with the 0072-era runtime-grants.sql, then 0073-0084), the same followed by a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql, and in new-installation order (0001-0084, then role bootstrap); every suite in services/ehr-api/database/tests (emergency.integration.sql included) and services/ehr-api/test/database passes in each, and the database/tests suites the rehearsal runs, with the new suite, pass under a non-superuser, NOBYPASSRLS definer owner. The new suite test/database/emergency-contacts.integration.sql fails at 0083 and passes at 0084; it shows break-glass committing when the feature's audit inserts fail and when its intent insert fails, an alert leased when its contact is removed or opted out and accepted afterwards recorded as delivered and audited, and notices the claim closes taking no slot in its batch, and catches each of 19 deliberate defects in 0084.
